summary: Official Sudan Aqari and NIC Spatial Portal sources were discovered and inspected. Aqari's current public route patterns were followed to bounded anonymous requests, but all tested API routes returned HTTP 500; the geoportal host did not resolve. No safe native parcel ID-plus-polygon response was qualified.
custodian: The Judicial Authority's Aqari platform is a national registration service; NIC's Sudan Spatial Portal is a national map-service project. No Umm Ruwaba-local registry custodian or local public parcel service was evidenced.
requests: Separate English and Arabic discovery, official page GETs, current Aqari JavaScript inspection, bounded anonymous API GETs, and the NIC geoportal route are recorded in the city record. No credentials, unsafe fields, CAPTCHA/Cloudflare bypass, or TLS disable was used.
safeFieldAllowlist: stable native parcel identifier only if source-proven
full parcel polygon geometry only when safely returned
scopeLimits: Exact WUP point [12.9073589794408, 31.2157543565926] and population 184761 persons are preserved.
No exact-point hit, API 500, DNS failure, or unavailable viewer is treated as citywide absence.
No raw source-specific attributes or GeoJSON sample were retained.
Packet completion is not source integration/admission.
uncertainty: Native parcel IDs, CRS, polygons, and citywide coverage remain unverified.
Aqari may require an authenticated workflow; the research did not attempt access beyond anonymous public GETs.
The geoportal may be temporarily unavailable or DNS-scoped outside this environment.
